# 1.2 Database Catalog Inspection (show dbs)

> "show dbs lists all databases on the MongoDB server that contain at least one collection, along with their size on disk. Databases that have only been selected with use (without any data written to them) will not appear here."

## 1. Operational Overview & Execution Context

To audit persisted databases across a MongoDB server instance, administrators execute `show dbs` in `mongosh`. This command inspects the server's storage catalog and outputs every database containing at least one materialized collection alongside its on-disk size in gigabytes.

Within the broader parent module (**1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle**), sub-topic `1.2` governs day-to-day developer workflows, driver execution behavior, and return telemetry.

## 2. Detailed Sub-Mechanism & Parameter Analysis

### 2.1 Command Syntax & Storage Footprint Output

Running `show dbs` (or its alias `show databases`) queries the server-wide catalog and prints each populated database alongside its formatted gigabyte size (e.g., `schoolDB 0.000GB`). Unlike `show collections`, `show dbs` inspects the entire server rather than just the active database.

### 2.2 Visibility Rules & Default System Partitions

Two rules govern `show dbs` output: (1) any database selected solely via `use` with zero written collections is omitted, and (2) every standard MongoDB server includes three pre-populated internal databases: `admin` (security/users), `config` (cluster/session metadata), and `local` (node-local data and oplog).

## 3. Production `mongosh` Workflows & Return Telemetry

The following `mongosh` implementation demonstrates practical operational patterns, parameter combinations, and server acknowledgment telemetry for this sub-topic.

```javascript
// Select a new database without writing to it
use stagingDB

// Inspect all persisted databases on the server
show dbs
// Output:
// admin      0.000GB
// config     0.000GB
// local      0.000GB
// schoolDB   0.000GB
// ("stagingDB" is omitted because it contains 0 collections)
```

Always inspect the acknowledgment object or return payload emitted by `mongosh` to confirm that your operation matched and affected the expected namespace or document set.

## 4. Operational Execution Pipeline Diagram

The architectural flowchart below traces the decision branches, parameter validations, and execution outcomes across the L-2 and L-3 mindmap nodes.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["1.2 show dbs"] --> B["Server-Wide Catalog Scan"]
    B --> C{"Has >= 1 Persisted Collection?"}
    C -->|Yes| D["Listed with Size in GB (schoolDB, admin, config, local)"]
    C -->|No| E["Excluded from Output (Unwritten use Pointers)"]
```

Understanding these operational branches prevents common runtime bugs during application development and database administration.

## 5. Multi-Dimension Comparison Matrix & Developer Pitfalls

| Database Namespace | Category | Primary Role | Visibility in `show dbs` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `admin` | System Database | Authentication, users, and admin commands | Always visible |
| `config` | System Database | Sharded cluster and session metadata | Always visible |
| `local` | System Database | Node-specific metadata and replication oplog | Always visible |
| `schoolDB` (populated) | Application DB | Stores user collections (`students`) | Visible once >= 1 collection exists |
| `stagingDB` (unwritten) | In-Memory Pointer | Selected via `use` without writes | Hidden |

### Key Exam Traps & Takeaways

- **Exam Trap — Why Is My Database Missing?**: The most common exam question asks why a database selected with `use myDB` does not appear in `show dbs`; the answer is that no collection or document has been written to it yet.
- **Server Scope vs. Database Scope**: `show dbs` operates at the server level regardless of which database is currently active.
- **Default System Trio**: Memorize the three default databases (`admin`, `config`, `local`).
